title: Lower the exponent 1/2 in Pasten's subexponential abc bound
credit: Extends H. Pasten, Invent. Math. 2024 (arXiv:2312.03566), Thm 1.4.
premise_risks: arXiv:2609.01327 (2026 preprint): cited in refs; M does not depend on it.
plain: Unconditionally, abc is known only in very weak forms. Pasten (2024) proved that if a ≤ c^{1−η} then log c ≤ η^{-1} exp(κ√(log R · log log R)), with R = rad(abc). abc predicts log c ≤ (1+ε) log R + O(1). Replace the square root by some smaller power of log R, in this bound or in Pasten's companion bound. Further questions (not part of the formal claim): just remove the log log R factor, i.e. get exp(O(√log R)).
math: For coprime positive $a+b=c$ with $R=\mathrm{rad}(abc)$, Pasten (Invent. Math. 2024, Thm 1.4) proves: (1) if $a\le c^{1-\eta}$ then $\log c\le \eta^{-1}\exp\big(\kappa\sqrt{\log R\,\log_2 R}\big)$; and (2) $\log c\le q\exp(\kappa\sqrt{\log R\log_2R})$ with $q=\min\{P(a),P(b),P(c)\}$. Claim: there is a fixed $\theta\in(0,1/2)$ such that (1) holds with $\exp(\kappa(\log R)^{\theta})$ for some $\kappa>0$ and all $\eta\in(0,1)$ and all triples, or (2) holds with $\exp(\kappa(\log R)^{\theta})$ for some $\kappa>0$ and all triples. Prove or disprove (a disproof would contradict abc). Further questions (not part of the formal claim): prove either statement with $\exp(O(\sqrt{\log R}))$.
